title: Intraoperative tumor detection during central nervous system surgery using optical coherence elastography (OCE)
summary:
Brain tumors often cannot be distinguished with sufficient accuracy from healthy brain tissue,  especially at the edges. In neurosurgery, therefore,  various tools are used to facilitate differentiation.  Preliminary studies on human brain tumor and brain tissue have shown that the mechanical properties of these tissues differ. This means that tumor tissue, for example, reacts differently to pressure than healthy brain tissue. In a collaboration between the University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein, Campus Lübeck, the Medical Laser Center Lübeck gGmbH, and the Institute for Biomedical Optics at the University of Lübeck, a system was developed that can display the mechanical properties of brain tumor tissue in contrast to healthy brain tissue. 
The developed system (name: AirJet-OCE) sends a slight air pulse to the tissue. At the same time, optical coherence tomography (OCT) is used to record the tissue reaction. OCT can be compared to ultrasound, but uses light instead of sound. This study is a feasibility study. The aim is to investigate whether the AirJet-OCE system can be used to visualize tissue differences during brain tumor surgery. This should help to preserve healthy tissue while still removing the tumor tissue as completely as possible.
conditions: Secondary malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified sites
Neoplasms of uncertain or unknown behaviour

interventions.name:
The study is single-arm, prospective, and diagnostic in design.
